title: Human Brain
subtitle: 1 SUB-ASSEMBLIES LOADED
overview: The human brain is a complex organ composed of several interconnected sub-structures that work together to process information and control bodily functions.

parts.name: Cerebral Cortex
parts.role: Surface layer responsible for sensory perception and motor control
summary: The cerebral cortex is a thin layer covering the surface of the brain, consisting of numerous folds called gyri and grooves called sulci.
It is responsible for processing sensory input and controlling voluntary movements.

parts.name: Basal Ganglia
parts.role: Control center for motor coordination and learning
summary: The basal ganglia is a group of nuclei located deep within the brain, involved in the regulation of movement and learning.
It receives signals from other parts of the brain and sends out commands to control muscle activity.

parts.name: Thalamus
parts.role: Central relay station for sensory information
summary: The thalamus is a structure located near the center of the brain, serving as a hub for transmitting sensory information to different areas of the brain.
It acts as a filter, prioritizing which sensory inputs reach higher brain regions.

parts.name: Pons
parts.role: Control center for sleep and arousal
summary: The pons is a structure located between the medulla oblongata and the midbrain, involved in regulating sleep and arousal states.
It helps maintain wakefulness and ensures proper sleep cycles.

parts.name: Medulla Oblongata
parts.role: Control center for basic life functions
summary: The medulla oblongata is a small structure located at the base of the brainstem, controlling essential life functions such as breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure.
It acts as a vital link between the central nervous system and the autonomic nervous system.

wikiSummary.title: Brain
wikiSummary.description: Organ central to the nervous system
wikiSummary.extract: The brain is an organ that serves as the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate and most invertebrate animals. It consists of nervous tissue and is typically located in the head (cephalization), usually near organs for special senses such as vision, hearing, and olfaction. Being the most specialized organ, it is responsible for receiving information from the sensory nervous system, processing that information and the coordination of motor control and the endocrine system.
